title: The lamp-room
text:
Rain on the skylight. The lamp sits cold in its housing, wick trimmed, ready since yesterday.

Aldis is not here. His coat is on the hook and it is still wet.

choices.label: Take the stairs to the gallery

title: Thirty years of weather
text:
He writes small and he writes every day. Wind, glass, swell. Who passed, and what it cost.

Somewhere in March: south stair rotten through, have written to the Board twice.

The last entry is four o'clock and it stops in the middle of a word. Boat off the Skerry standing too far in. No answer to the horn. Taking the north stair down to

The pen is uncapped beside it.

choices.label: Take the stairs to the gallery

title: The boat store
text:
Paraffin, and a spare pane wrapped in sacking. The oil lamp is under the bench on the third shelf where it has always been.

Aldis's boots are still on the peg. Whatever he went down in, he went down in his shoes.

choices.label: Take the stairs to the gallery

title: The gallery
text:
The wind takes the door out of your hand. Below, the sea goes over the Skerry in long white sheets.

There is a light on the water. It sits where no light should sit, and it is not moving the way a boat under way moves.

Then a shout from the rocks under the north stair. Twice. The second one is weaker.

You are afraid. What frightens you is how long you stand there doing the arithmetic.

choices.label: Light the oil lamp first, then take the north stair

title: What the light is for
text:
You light it. The beam goes out and swings and on the third pass the boat comes round hard and finds the channel.

Four men you will never meet go home.

The tide drops at six. Aldis is at the foot of the north stair, and he is still holding the horn.

title: What you carry up
text:
You go down. The stair is wet, the rock is worse, and he is heavier than a man that thin has any right to be.

You get him up to the lamp-room. He is breathing. His leg is wrong below the knee.

Behind you, out in the dark, the Skerry takes the boat. You hear it go. There is nothing to see, because there is no light.

title: The north stair
text:
The oil lamp is under the bench on the third shelf, where the log says it lives. Lit, carried up, hung on the gallery rail: four minutes.

Then the north stair, because the log says the south one is rotten through and he has been writing to the Board about it since March.

The boat comes round. You get him up.

He does not thank you. He lies on the lamp-room floor with his leg strapped, looking at the ceiling, and says: thirty years, and a relief off the boat reads my log and does it in twenty minutes.

The supply does not come for three days. It is a small room.
